verdict.rationale: Slack documents first-party developer sandboxes. These are separate Enterprise org environments of two or more workspaces for building against all Slack features 'safely and securely' at no extra cost, explicitly framed as building 'without putting production at risk'. This is true environment isolation, not a dry-run mode. The documentation in the pack is thin, though. Missing for 10: details on provisioning and seeding test data, sandbox limits or lifetime, how sandbox credentials are kept separate from production, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: A developer sandbox is an Enterprise org environment (a network of two or more Slack workspace instances) that can be used to build against all Slack features safely and securely
Empower teams to build without putting production at risk
that can be used to build against all Slack features safely and securely, without an additional cost.
